haiku-low.q1: Its document is deleted from the index. Any status other than active becomes a delete of that product's document.
haiku-low.q2: The store rejects the older write with a version-conflict error. It is counted as stale, not an error, and the newer data stays.
haiku-low.q3: It retries the same batch, waiting 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and so on, capped at 60 s. It never skips ahead, so lag grows and ops should alert on lag.
haiku-low.q4: It is sent to topic catalog.products.dlq with the document and error, an alert is raised, and processing continues. The product's later changes still flow.
haiku-low.q5: An alert fires at 20 GB of retained WAL. At 50 GB ops drop the slot, change capture breaks, some changes never reach Kafka, and only a full rebuild restores a correct index.
haiku-low.q6: Search reads only the alias, which moves atomically to products_v4. This happens only when lag is under 5 s and the count is within 0.5% of active rows.
haiku-low.q7: In Kafka consumer offsets. An offset advances only after the index has acknowledged every write up to that offset.
haiku-low.q8: It re-reads from the last committed offset. Repeated writes are harmless because the version rule rejects the older copies.
haiku-low.q9: A catch-up consumer reads the topic from the recorded offsets and applies the same rules as live sync to products_v4 until the switch.
haiku-low.q10: Version S, the WAL position read inside the snapshot transaction.
haiku-low.q11: For 48 hours after the switch, every change is written to both v4 and v3, with offsets committed only after both acknowledge. Rollback moves the alias back to v3. After 48 hours, products_v3 is deleted and writes to it stop.
haiku-low.q12: Search is unaffected and stays on products_v3, since nothing half-built is visible. A backfill crash needs a second snapshot, which needs DBA approval. If the catch-up falls behind, do not switch; keep catching up and alert.

sonnet.q1: The indexer deletes that product's document from the index (any non-active status becomes a delete).
sonnet.q2: The older change has a lower version (commit_lsn), so the store rejects it with a version-conflict error. The indexer counts it as stale, not an error, and moves on. The newer data stays.
sonnet.q3: It retries the same batch, waiting 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and so on, capped at 60 s. It never skips ahead and does not commit offsets. Sync stops and lag grows, so you alert on lag.
sonnet.q4: The document and the error go to the DLQ topic catalog.products.dlq, an alert is raised, and processing continues. The product's later changes still flow.
sonnet.q5: At 50 GB ops drop the replication slot. Change capture is then broken and some changes never reach Kafka. Only a full rebuild (new index via the rebuild job) restores a correct index.
sonnet.q6: The alias products is moved to products_v4 in one atomic step. Before that, lag must be under 5 seconds and the document count in products_v4 must be within 0.5% of the active row count.
sonnet.q7: In Kafka consumer offsets. An offset is committed only after the index has acknowledged every write up to that offset (after both indexes during the 48-hour dual-write period).
sonnet.q8: It re-reads from the last committed offset. Repeated writes are harmless because the version rule rejects the older copy.
sonnet.q9: The job first records each partition's Kafka offset. A catch-up consumer then reads the topic from those offsets and applies the same rules as live sync to products_v4. Changes after S have a higher version and replace copied rows. Older replayed changes are rejected as stale.
sonnet.q10: Version S, the WAL position read inside the snapshot transaction, as a number.
sonnet.q11: For 48 hours after the switch, every change is written to both products_v4 and products_v3, and an offset is committed only after both acknowledge. So v3 stays current and rollback is just moving the alias back. After 48 hours, products_v3 is deleted and writing to it stops.
sonnet.q12: Search is unaffected. It stays on products_v3 through the alias until the switch, and nothing half-built is visible. (A crash during the backfill needs a second snapshot, which needs approval. If approval is refused, stop and re-plan with the DBA.)
